tiles.title: Configure secure human access with temporary credentials

blocks.text: Permissions are made available through IAM Identity Center permission-set assignments to users or groups in specified AWS accounts. An operator needs approved access, not saved long-lived IAM user keys.

Use the supplied assignment workflow to assign the approved user or group, account and permission set. Then sign in to that account and test the intended access. Keep the assignment, signed-in permission-set context and test result together: sign-in alone is not the complete access check.

For cedar-operator in cedar-operators, compare the assigned account and permission set with the approved context. The intended test is read sandbox evidence object. Keep its expected and observed results alongside the signed-in context.

Configure a named SSO profile with aws configure sso. Establish its session with aws sso login --profile NAME, replacing NAME with the profile name. Use this session workflow rather than storing long-lived IAM user keys.

tiles.title: Configure security groups after external ports/firewall preparation

blocks.text: Security groups contain allow rules evaluated at associated network interfaces, not explicit deny rules.

They are stateful: responses to allowed connections are allowed regardless of response-direction rules. Add inbound rules for the required protocol, port range and approved source; remove unnecessary ingress, then test required connections and responses.

blocks.title: Connection, tracked response and filtering boundary

edges.label: Alternative inbound rule: allow TCP 443 from sg-cedar-source; no rule import.

blocks.alt_text: Connection, tracked response and filtering boundary

blocks.text: Use the supplied TCP ingress rule and approved source on the workload’s associated security group. Remove unnecessary ingress and test both the required connection and its response. A tracked response is allowed regardless of response-direction rules; a new connection from an unapproved source is a different case. Do not widen ingress to make an unexplained test pass.

A security-group ID used as an allowed source identifies that source; it does not import the referenced group’s rules into the destination group. Security groups contain allow rules, not explicit deny rules.

Security groups do not filter traffic to Amazon-provided DNS or EC2 instance metadata services. Those cases are outside the filtering boundary, so their results do not demonstrate that ordinary ingress is allowed.

tiles.title: Evaluate resource-based permissions for a requested operation

steps.title: Match a request to its resource policy

blocks.text: A resource-based policy is attached to a resource and specifies the principals, actions and resources covered by its statements.

For an S3 bucket policy, compare Principal, Action, Resource and Condition with the request. Bucket and object ARNs have different scopes. Same-account identity and resource permissions can contribute allows; applicable explicit denies override them. Cross-account access generally requires permission on both sides.

blocks.title: Caller, statement fields and distinct ARN scopes

blocks.text: Compare the caller with Principal, the operation with Action, the object ARN with Resource, and request values with Condition. A bucket ARN is not automatically the scope of an object request. A resource policy includes principal scope; it is not just an identity policy moved to another file.

Use the supplied permission evidence alongside the field matches. In a same-account request, identity and resource permissions can contribute allows, but an applicable explicit deny overrides them. For cross-account access, permission is generally required on both sides. Keep that qualification: the supplied ordinary cases are not an exhaustive account of special cases.

tiles.title: Execute an established managed account-onboarding workflow

blocks.text: Account Factory provisions and enrolls accounts into a governed landing zone using standardized account settings. The onboarding request supplies approved inputs and baseline checkpoints; creation is only part of the task.

Execute the established provisioning workflow with the approved account inputs. Inspect enrollment and organizational-unit placement, then verify each supplied baseline checkpoint against evidence of the account’s applied controls. Do not invent new baseline controls.

If the account was created but a checkpoint has no supporting result, record that distinction. Creation, enrollment and placement do not replace the checkpoint comparison. A created account alone does not demonstrate governance completion.
